candidate.answerReason: Equal vertical included angles and the two equal side pairs give congruent triangles AOB and COD by SAS. Their corresponding sides AB and CD are equal, so CD=7.

methods.label: Vertical angles and SAS
methods.explanation: \(\angle AOB=\angle COD\) (vertically opposite angles), \(OA=OC\), and \(OB=OD\), so \(\triangle AOB\cong\triangle COD\) by SAS. Thus, \(CD=AB=7\).
methods.levelReason: Vertical angles, SAS, and corresponding sides of congruent triangles are within Grades 7–8.

methods.label: Recognize a parallelogram
methods.explanation: The equalities \(OA=OC\) and \(OB=OD\) show that \(O\) is the midpoint of both \(AC\) and \(BD\). These are the diagonals of quadrilateral \(ABCD\), so its diagonals bisect each other. A quadrilateral whose diagonals bisect each other is a parallelogram. Its opposite sides are equal, giving \(CD=AB=7\).
methods.levelReason: The midpoint interpretation and parallelogram criterion and properties are all in the supplied Grade 8 scope.

needsNewNodes.name: Equal connector lengths in a common-midpoint configuration
needsNewNodes.description: For two noncollinear segments AC and BD sharing midpoint O, establish that the connectors AB and CD have equal lengths and determine either length from the other. Triangle congruence and parallelogram recognition are alternative proof routes.
needsNewNodes.reason: cnm_055 covers direct segment comparison, segment arithmetic, and midpoints. cnm_121 and cnm_183 describe the separate proof routes; neither represents the common task target without prescribing a route.
